runs.answer: Affected banks: Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Capital One, with US Bank and PNC added later Monday, plus spillover delays on Zelle (UPI, NY Post, Fox Business all covered it). runs.answer: Germany 5-0 Netherlands, UEFA Nations League A Group A2, Olympiastadion Berlin, Mon 16 Nov 2026 (HT 1-0). runs.title: The Simpsons' 17 Nov blackout rumour: true or not?
runs.prompt: There is a viral rumour that The Simpsons predicted a worldwide power blackout on 17 November 2026, tied to a FEMA test. Find out what the rumour actually claims, which Simpsons episode (if any) it references, and whether fact-checkers or official sources (e.g. FEMA) have debunked or confirmed it. Start from The Independent's explainer at https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/simpsons-blackout-theory-17-november-b3085604.html and one other debunking source. Give the verdict and any official position.
runs.answer: The rumour claims a 2023 Simpsons episode predicted a worldwide blackout on 17 November 2026, tied to a US emergency-alert/FEMA test. It references Season 35, episode 7, "It's a Blunderful Life" (first aired 19 November 2023), in which an aged Lisa, 60 years in the future, recalls a blackout that began on November 17 and left the fictional town of Springfield without power for six days — posts clipped that scene (some said "watch the last 15 seconds") and recast a local cartoon outage as a global prophecy; the episode never mentions 2026 or a worldwide blackout. Fact-checkers rate it false: Parade's explainer, Brazilian checker boatos.org/Lupa ("It is false that The Simpsons predicted a global blackout on November 17, 2026"), The Mirror ("debunked") and other fact-checks find no evidence and call the date coincidence. The only real 17 November 2026 event is official and routine: FEMA, in coordination with the FCC, runs a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System that day at about 2:20 p.m. ET (back-up date 3 December 2026) — a broadcast of a warning message over radio, TV, cable and satellite, not a power cut, and FEMA has announced nothing resembling a blackout.

runs.title: Delta CEO: flights slower than the 1950s — the claim
runs.prompt: Delta CEO Ed Bastian recently called it 'absurd' that the Atlanta (ATL) to New York LaGuardia (LGA) flight takes longer today than in the 1950s, blaming outdated air traffic control. Find out what he actually said, what argument or comparison he made about flight times then vs now, and what he is calling for (e.g. FAA or ATC changes). Use public reporting such as Fortune and any non-paywalled summary. Report the substance of the claim and the remedy he proposes.
runs.answer: At the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum (Nov 2026), Delta CEO Ed Bastian said it's "absurd" that the Atlanta–LaGuardia flight Delta launched in the 1950s still takes longer today than it did then, blaming congested, outdated U.S. air traffic control rather than aircraft: jets have improved enormously, but "the one thing that hasn't changed at the pace that it needs to is the skies." He first made the comparison in a May 2025 TODAY interview, calling the system "very slow" and "congested," saying the controller screens "look like something out of the 1960s and '70s," and noting radar/radio equipment dating to the 1960s — while insisting flying remains "absolutely safe" because of the skill of controllers and pilots. His remedy is a federally funded overhaul of ATC/NextGen: retiring aging radar and radio for satellite/GPS-based navigation, modern communications and modernized control centers, and he presses Congress, the FAA and DOT (Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy) to commit the roughly $50 billion needed to modernize the system before capacity constraints worsen.

runs.answer: Pick: the USA Today live blog (usatoday.com/story/money/2026/11/16/bank-outage-nationwide-chase-bofa--live/92814152007/). runs.title: Pick the best NCAA women's soccer tournament source
runs.prompt: The 2026 NCAA Division I women's soccer championship selection show and bracket schedule were just released. Choose which single public page is the best place to get the full bracket, schedule and selection-show details. Candidate pages: NCAA.com's official page (https://www.ncaa.com/news/soccer-women/article/2026-11-09/2026-di-womens-soccer-championship-selection-show-info-bracket-schedule), Sporting News (https://www.sportingnews.com/us/college/news/ncaa-womens-soccer-schedule-2026-channels-times-streams-scores/c73e72915d4e31dc5cf6deec), and the Yahoo Sports selection-show live coverage (https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/ncaa-womens-soccer-selection-show-200039281.html). Name your pick and justify it (completeness, readability, free access).
runs.answer: Pick the NCAA.com page: it's the official, free hub and it redirected to the canonical "2026 DI women's soccer championship: Bracket, schedule, scores" page, which carried a link to the interactive 64-team bracket plus all 32 first-round matchups with dates and times (Nov. 20-22), the second/third round (Nov. 27 and Nov. 30), quarterfinals (Dec. 5), Women's College Cup (Dec. 10 and 13 on ESPNU), the selection-show detail (4 p.m. ET Monday, Nov. 16 streamed on NCAA.com) and past champions. It's plain text, readable and paywall-free. Sporting News promises "every college game" with TV channels and times but its article body was buried under a huge navigation/ad wrapper and didn't render in text; Yahoo's piece is only a "live updates" story (4 min read) whose body didn't render either, leaving just the headline, byline and recommended links.
obstacles: Yahoo live-blog body did not render in text extraction; only headline/byline/recommended stories were visible

runs.title: Pick the best Sam Hartman Bachelor source
runs.prompt: The Bachelor season 30 will star NFL quarterback Sam Hartman, a surprise choice. Choose which single non-paywalled article gives the clearest, most complete account of who Sam Hartman is and why he was named the next Bachelor. Candidate pages: Entertainment Weekly (https://ew.com/who-is-the-bachelor-season-30-nfl-quarterback-sam-hartman-12252580), People (https://people.com/all-about-sam-hartman-the-bachelor-season-30-12252745), and Sports Illustrated (https://www.si.com/onsi/athlete-lifestyle/nfl-quarterback-sam-hartman-named-the-next-bachelor-in-surprising-career-twist). Name your pick and justify it briefly (background detail, free to read, clear facts).
runs.answer: Pick Sports Illustrated (On SI), by Maggie MacKenzie. It's the only one of the three that is actually free to read — both EW and People returned HTTP 402 access blocks in my browser. SI's piece is also the most complete: it dates ABC's announcement (Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, via joint Instagram post), gives the March 21, 2027 Season 30 premiere, and lays out who Hartman is — the 27-year-old Washington Commanders QB who spent five seasons at Wake Forest, transferred to Notre Dame for 2023, threw for 15,000+ yards and 134 touchdowns, went undrafted in 2024, signed with Washington as a UDFA and spent time on the practice squad, and previously appeared on Netflix's QB1. It also explains the "why": an active NFL QB is a surprise pick, fans reacted with revived interest, and host Jesse Palmer (the show's fifth Bachelor in 2004) set the QB-to-Bachelor precedent.

People returned the same HTTP 402 access block
